neighbours.label: the word just before a back-reference to something already mentioned (shores of [this], buy [that], use [the same])
fire: A small pond lies behind the farm, and every winter the surface of this pond freezes solid.
An old oak stood in the square; children climbed the branches of this tree for decades.
I saw a red bicycle in the shop window and knew I had to buy that bicycle.
There was a rare orchid in the valley, but grazing led to the disappearance of this plant.
The village had a single well, and families drew water out of this well each morning.
He got a strange letter on Monday, but the content of this letter was never revealed.
A tiny bakery opened downtown, and the owner of this bakery is my cousin.
She wiped the counter with a rag and then used the same rag on the table.
quiet: Behind the farm the land is flat, and every winter the surface of a pond freezes solid.
In the square the children climbed the branches of trees for decades.
Walking past the shop window I decided I needed to buy a new bicycle.
In the valley, grazing has led to the disappearance of many plants.
In the village families drew water out of wells each morning.
On Monday the content of most letters was about the weather.
Downtown is busy, and the owners of most bakeries rise early.
She wiped the counter with a rag and then wiped the table with a sponge.

notes: Top: ' of' x13 almost always followed by 'this' referring back to an earlier noun. The activation precedes the demonstrative, so the test varies whether a referent was introduced earlier. Low confidence.
